checks.detail: rays.i(coated)/rays.i(uncoated) equals 0.01*x + 0.5 at surfaces.x[1, :] to 1.110e-16, but differs from the same formula at the image plane by up to 1.552e-01. The `rays` a coating receives carry the coated surface's coordinates, before further propagation -- confirmed independently by capturing rays.x inside transmit().
checks.name: the_coating_sees_the_coated_surfaces_coordinates

checks.detail: comparing the ABSOLUTE rays.i against the coating's own formula misses by 3.082e-03: the uncoated downstream surfaces contribute their own ray-dependent factor (the same effect recorded in t18). A custom coating can only be validated against a matched uncoated trace.
checks.name: the_coatings_value_must_be_read_relative_to_an_uncoated_baseline

checks.detail: with the same coating on both lens surfaces, rays.i equals 0.01*x + 0.5 at the SECOND surface ALONE to 0.000e+00 -- exactly, with no residual factor, because the last coating to run assigns rather than multiplies. The first surface's contribution is gone. `rays.i = ...` overwrites; a composable coating must use `rays.i *= ...`.
checks.name: an_assigning_coating_discards_the_rays_prior_intensity

checks.detail: the observed transmission ratios 0.45um 0.402500, 0.55um 0.502500, 0.65um 0.622500 match lambda_um^2 + 0.2 and are nowhere near lambda_nm^2 + 0.2, so rays.w is in micrometres -- the same unit as Optic.trace's wavelength argument
checks.name: rays_w_is_the_wavelength_in_micrometres

checks.detail: the per-ray transmission ratio has zero spread at each wavelength, as a function of rays.w alone must
checks.name: the_spectral_coating_is_wavelength_flat_across_the_pupil

checks.detail: transmission rises with wavelength as lambda^2 + 0.2 requires: 0.402500 < 0.502500 < 0.622500
checks.name: the_spectral_coating_is_monotonic_in_wavelength

checks.detail: a coating assigning rays.i = 1.5 yields a transmittance of 1.500000 relative to the uncoated trace. Optiland neither clamps nor warns.
checks.name: a_custom_coating_can_set_a_transmittance_above_one

checks.detail: a coating assigning rays.i = -0.25 yields -0.250000. Negative intensity is accepted silently, so a custom coating carries the entire burden of energy conservation -- the tutorial's own GradientCoating is unphysical for |x| > 50 mm for exactly this reason.
checks.name: a_custom_coating_can_set_a_negative_transmittance

demonstrates: subclassing coatings.BaseCoating with transmit(rays, nx, ny, nz) and reflect(...), and the fact that the `rays` handed to a coating carry the coordinates of the coated surface and rays.w in micrometres.
title: Custom Coating Types
